problem: Suppose $X$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $det(X)=-48.$ The matrix $Y$ is obtained from $X$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3}.$ What is the value of $det(Y)?$

activity_context.topic_title: Row and Column Operations on Determinants

feedback.problem: Suppose $C$ is a $9\times 9$ matrix and $det(C)=-93.$ The matrix $D$ is obtained from $C$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{9}:=-\frac{5}{31}{R}_{9}.$ What is the value of $det(D)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The row operation applied to $C$ consists of multiplying a row by the number $-\frac{5}{31}.$

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(D) & =-\frac{5}{31}det(C) \\  & =-\frac{5}{31}\cdot (-93) \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$
